summary: Pisgah National Forest lookout off the Blue Ridge Parkway: built 1931 or 1932 (sources differ), staffed through the 1970s, restored 1996; cab locked, trail and stairs open.

facts.design: 32-foot steel tower with a wooden cab and catwalk in a steep pyramid-roof design (Register)
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Appalachian Ranger District (Register)

access.note: Trail and overlook are public. The top cab is locked: TEHCC says locked for restoration (undated revision), and Romantic Asheville says the Forest Service opens it only for special tours. The stairs remain as a viewpoint. The Forest Service Green Knob Trail page shows an undated 'Temporarily closed due to storm damage' notice, scope unclear.

visit.trail_note: About half a mile from the Green Knob Overlook at Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 350.4; the top cab is not open to visitors. The Forest Service 2.8-mile Green Knob Trail page shows a temporary storm-damage closure notice, undated.

events.note: Register and TEHCC: built by the CCC and USFS (TEHCC credits the CCC) in 1932. Romantic Asheville and CNY Hiking give 1931.
Staffed 'through the 1970s' per two blogs; the decade only is given, so 1970 is a placeholder for the decade
Register says restored in 1996; Romantic Asheville and CNY Hiking say repaired in 1996
Cab restored in 2013 per Romantic Asheville
Registered March 1, 1998; nominated by R. Fred Foster, North Carolina Registrar

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register credits the CCC and USFS with building it in 1932; TEHCC credits the CCC alone with 1932. Romantic Asheville and CNY Hiking say the Forest Service built it in 1931. No primary record was read. The story reports the disagreement and does not choose.
The Register says Yancey County; a North Carolina tower list says McDowell County. The brief record uses Yancey. The story reports both.

sources.title: Green Knob Lookout Tower, Blue Ridge Parkway

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict (1931 vs 1932) is unresolved; the Register and TEHCC say 1932. County conflict (Yancey vs McDowell) is unresolved. The 1996 restoration matches across the Register and two blogs. Current cab closure comes from a blog and an undated wiki revision; verify before publishing. The Forest Service Green Knob Trail page shows a 'Temporarily closed due to storm damage' notice under Current Conditions; no date or scope, so the story now says so. Two blogs say the tower is on the National Register of Historic Places; not verified, not used. Outbound calls the tower abandoned; not used. Facebook posts not cited. Staffing history rests on two blogs; no current volunteer schedule found. Page reads: 7 distinct pages, one over the 6-page budget.
